problem: Prior open-vocabulary navigation/manipulation work assumes static environments, fixed tabletop arms, or simulation-only settings, and cannot exploit environment semantics to cope with unseen scenes, object relocation and unreliable user hints on real mobile platforms.
motivation: Real-world mobile manipulators must operate in unseen, dynamic environments where objects move and user hints may be wrong. Pretrained VLMs/LLMs give zero-shot detection and commonsense reasoning, so a semantic map of instances and abstract regions can guide where to search first and how to replan on failure without any training.
key_idea: Build a 3-layer 3D semantic map (SLAM structure, VLM-detected instances, LLM-abstracted regions) and use an LLM to rank regions by semantic relevance to the target and user hints, so a training-free robot searches regions in order and replans to the next most likely region.
insight: Semantic region prioritization sharply raises first-trial success over random region ordering (SFT 73.33% NoHint and 100% Hinting vs 23.34% Random), and improves SPL. Failure recovery works because the ordered region list acts as a fallback: even with misleading hints or objects in irrelevant regions, navigation success stays 86.67%, though SPL drops below random. This shows the method depends on the reliability of the hints and of commonsense semantics for efficiency, not for eventual success.
method: Heuristic exploration and structural layer: frontier exploration with ORB-SLAM RGB-D-inertial builds keyframe poses and accumulates dense depth point clouds as the structural layer, flattened to 2D cost maps for navigation

Instance semantic layer: Grounded SAM (Grounding DINO/Detic + SAM) segments open-vocabulary instances per keyframe, prompts are proposed by InternVL 1.5; masks are lifted to 3D points to form semantic geometric instances (label, center, relative geometry) registered on the map

Abstract region layer: instances are projected to a BEV map, a circular sliding window collects object labels, and GPT-4o proposes ranked region labels for each window, giving a dense zero-shot region map R(x,y)

Instruction parsing and region prioritization: GPT-4o parses the instruction into target object and optional hinted region, ranks the scene's regions by semantic relevance to the target, then reprioritizes the hinted region to the top

Prioritized navigation and in-region search: precomputed reachability-based searchable locations per region, A*/OMPL global planner with DWA local planner, visiting regions in ranked order until the target is found

Proposal-approval detection and grasping: Grounded SAM proposes detections for the target and InternVL double-checks to cut false positives; the highest-confidence approved instance is grasped with sampling-based arm planning (up to 3 trials per location), then the robot returns to the user

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen, LLM), Grounded SAM (Grounding DINO + SAM, frozen), InternVL 1.5 (frozen); region abstraction also demonstrated with LLaMA 3
setting.observation: RGB-D camera near the end-effector plus IMU, used for SLAM
setting.action_space: Planned base navigation (A* global + DWA local) to searchable locations and predefined camera view poses; sampling-based arm motion planning for grasp
setting.privileged: Semantic map pre-built in a prior mapping stage of the same scene (exploration/mapping done before task episodes); predefined camera view angles per location; list of scene regions; hand-designed placements

numbers.extra: Real robot JSR-1, 5 regions and 20 object categories, in-house 200 m2 space; SFT/SPL improvement measured against the Random-order control group

numbers_note: Custom real-world benchmark only; no standard benchmarks. Random-order control (30 eps): SFT 23.34, SN 86.67, SP 76.67, Succ. 76.67, SPL 0.5332. Abstract's 'average 76.67% on replanning' is not clearly derived from tables. Text says 135 episodes but the group counts sum to 135 including Random (105 without).
results: On 105 real-robot episodes the method reaches 80.95% navigation and 73.33% overall success, with SFT and SPL improved by 157.18% and 19.53% over a random region-order control. Hints yield 100% SFT; misleading hints or misplaced objects drop SPL below control but the robot still recovers, with 86.67% SN.
limitations: Evaluation is only in one in-house scene with 5 regions and 20 object categories, with no comparison to other published systems, only a random-order baseline
Assumes a pre-built map (autonomous exploration is left to future work), predefined camera view angles, and a single target per type; efficiency degrades with misleading hints
Detailed component ablations and failure analysis (e.g. grasp failures, false positives) are missing; overall success is only 73%
